name: Halyard Engineering
description: The engineering blog of Halyard, the webhook delivery platform. Postmortems with real numbers and design writeups with real code, written by the engineers on call.

masthead.headline: Notes from the team that keeps nine million webhooks a day moving.
masthead.dek: Postmortems with real numbers. Design writeups with real code. This is how we build — and occasionally break — the delivery pipeline.
meta: Written by the engineers on call
New posts when there is something to say

writing.heading: Writing
writing.lede: Everything we have published, newest first. Series posts are threaded — follow the crimson line.

about.heading: About this blog
paragraphs: Halyard delivers webhooks for commerce and billing platforms — about nine million a day, from checkout events to subscription renewals. This blog is the paper trail: when something breaks we publish the postmortem, and when we build something worth copying we publish the design.
We write the way we run incidents — plain language, real numbers, and code you can check. Nothing here is ghostwritten, and nothing goes through marketing.

faq.heading: Questions we get
faq.lede: How this blog works, in four answers.

items.question: Who writes the posts?
items.answer: The engineers who did the work. Every draft gets a technical review from someone else on the incident or project, and one edit for clarity. Nothing is ghostwritten and nothing goes through marketing.

items.question: Can I republish or translate a post?
items.answer: Yes. Republish or translate any post with attribution and a link to the original. The code snippets are MIT-licensed — use them without asking.

items.question: Do you publish a postmortem for every incident?
items.answer: We publish when customers felt the impact or when the failure taught us something transferable. Internal-only incidents get the same written review; it just stays internal.

items.question: Do you take guest posts or sponsorships?
items.answer: No. Everything here was written by someone at Halyard, about systems we run in production. That is the whole editorial policy.

footer.note: Halyard moves webhooks for commerce and billing platforms. The engineering team writes here.
